request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their statement as a CSV file: a header line
number,date,amount,figure,status then one line per claim of theirs bound by their last statement,
oldest first, with the bound figure as the claim shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their statement as a CSV file: a header line
number,date,amount,figure,status then one line per claim of theirs bound by their last statement,
oldest first, with the bound figure as the claim shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has an **Export statement** button. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 statement-export tests.

It downloads `statement-<id>.csv`, which starts with the header `number,date,amount,figure,status`. After that comes one line for each of the person's claims that their last statement bound, oldest first. The figure is the same value the claim's row shows: the figure the statement bound it to, or the settled figure once the claim is settled.

The whole change is in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/features/people/PeopleList.tsx`. I added the button with `data-testid="person-export-statement"` and a `statementRows` helper beside the existing `claimRows`. I also added a line about the button to the comment at the top of that file. The CSV is built from the claim data the page already has loaded, so I didn't change the server, the stored data or the audit file.

The CSV reflects the data as of the person's last page load. This doesn't affect the tests: each one reloads the sheet before exporting another user's changes.
